units.title: Stable and online softmax, normalization and fused residual paths
outcomes: Integrate residual-add plus RMSNorm with explicit mutation, accumulation and epsilon contracts.
Use online-softmax state to combine disjoint decode partitions without averaging their outputs.
Test both returned activations and retained residuals against an independent reference.
units.why: Build on Online softmax state, query and key-value tiling and Stable RMSNorm and LayerNorm, and RoPE fusion. The serving task is preserving residual state and reduction semantics across repeated decode steps, not writing another generic reduction kernel.

next.note: Apply the reduction contract to serving attention shapes.

study.title: Attention composition, arXiv:2501.01005v1
study.locator: Section 2.2, Attention Composition, attention-state definition and binary merge
study.depth: Use disjoint key subsets and maximum subtraction when merging. Associativity holds in real arithmetic, not bitwise floating-point arithmetic.

study.title: Fused residual mutation contract
study.locator: FlashInfer 0.7.1 documentation: Step 1, Step 2 and Parameters of `fused_add_rmsnorm`

study.title: Residual ownership in the model path
study.locator: `RMSNormFused.forward`, including the absent-residual branch

focus: For residual sum \(z=x+r\), RMSNorm returns \(w\odot z/\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}(z^2)+\epsilon}\). LayerNorm instead centers the row and uses population variance. Preserve the model's choice.
The fused API overwrites the residual with the sum and the input with normalized activations. Returning only normalized values loses state needed by the next block.
For partial attention states, merge unnormalized weights or log-normalizers. Keep the logarithm base consistent and rescale by the larger maximum before exponentiating.
Specify whether the residual sum is rounded to storage dtype before normalization. Promotion before the sum and promotion only for the reduction are different numerical contracts.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, implement a CPU double-precision residual/RMSNorm reference with `eps=1e-6`. For input `[1., 2., 3., 4.]`, residual `[4., 3., 2., 1.]` and unit weights, the retained residual is `[5., 5., 5., 5.]`; RMSNorm is approximately one while centered LayerNorm is zero. Check both buffers through two successive calls. Then merge disjoint online-softmax states from your earlier GPU-track implementation and compare with one dense reduction under its declared tolerance.
traps: Validating activations but forgetting that the residual was overwritten incorrectly.
Reading aliased input and residual buffers as though they were independent. Reject unsupported overlap before dispatch.
Initializing an all-masked partition with ordinary subtraction of two negative infinities. Give empty states an explicit identity path.

selfTest.q: Why is averaging two partition outputs wrong?
selfTest.a: Their softmax denominators generally differ. Weight each output by its partition's normalizer before dividing by the combined normalizer.

selfTest.q: Does finite-logit maximum subtraction make every softmax input safe?
selfTest.a: No. NaNs, positive infinities and all-masked rows still need a declared policy. A finite nonempty row avoids exponential overflow after subtraction.

selfTest.q: What must a residual-fusion oracle return?
selfTest.a: The updated residual and normalized activation, with the intended cast points, epsilon, weight and mutation semantics.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: `servelab` residual-state and split-softmax reference checks, including repeated calls and empty partitions.
units.stopWhen: Both residual and activation pass independent repeated-call checks, and split-softmax merges match the dense oracle under a stated finite and all-masked policy.

fit.note: Kept: attention composition, the fused API and the runner's residual branches cover the serving contract; the mini-project supplies repeated-state practice.

units.title: Prefill and decode attention shapes and IO-aware attention
outcomes: Derive rectangular attention shapes for uncached prefill, cached chunks and ordinary decode.
Separate query-head arithmetic from KV-head traffic and identify potential GQA reuse.
Predict when query tiling or split-KV parallelism is worth testing without assuming a bandwidth bottleneck.
units.why: Attention shapes, prefill and decode reuse, and materialized traffic already supplied the square-attention ledger. Serving adds cached suffixes, mixed request lengths and a shape distribution that can invalidate a single-kernel choice.

next.note: Carry logical shapes into physical page addressing.

study.title: Serving intensity and tile selection, arXiv:2501.01005v1
study.locator: Section 2.1, FlashAttention; Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.2, data movement and microkernel tile sizes; Appendix A, Head Group Fusion for Grouped-Query Attention
study.depth: Use the paper's intensity as an attention-only model. Its statement about batching does not apply to weight reuse in the rest of a transformer.

study.title: Forward attention state and work
study.locator: Section 4.2.2, Details of the FlashAttention forward pass and Algorithm 1, printed pp. 24 to 25
study.depth: Reuse your completed forward implementation. Skip backward and the training benchmark sweep; extend the shape ledger to rectangular cached attention.

focus: For one request with \(q\) query tokens, \(s\) visible KV tokens, \(H_q\) query heads and head width \(d\), scores have shape \(H_q	imes q	imes s\). Uncached prefill has equal lengths; a cached chunk has more keys than queries; ordinary decode has one query.
Dense score and value products cost \(4H_q qsd\) FLOPs, counting a multiply-add as two. This excludes scaling, masking and softmax; useful causal pairs and executed padded tiles need separate counts.

An ideal single KV read costs \(2H_{kv}sd b\) bytes for equal key/value widths and \(b\) bytes per element. Reusing these bytes across grouped heads is a schedule property, not a consequence of fewer stored heads alone.
IO-aware attention removes global score/probability materialization. Short queries still offer little query-row reuse; split-KV adds parallelism but needs partial-state storage and reduction.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, draw a request with 5 cached tokens and a 3-token chunk, four query heads, two KV heads and width 8. Scores are \(4	imes3	imes8\); the three query rows allow 6, 7 and 8 keys respectively. Derive 3072 dense-product FLOPs versus 2688 useful causal-product FLOPs, and 512 bytes for one ideal KV read with two-byte storage. Keep query/output bytes, softmax work, metadata and actual reloads outside that KV-only count.
traps: Using a square or upper-left causal mask for a cached suffix. Its query positions start after the cached prefix.
Reducing arithmetic by the GQA group size. Query heads still compute distinct scores and outputs.
Calling a low-intensity attention shape bandwidth-bound without timings and profiler evidence. Launch supply or insufficient parallelism may dominate.

selfTest.q: Does batching unrelated decode requests create reuse of each request's KV across query tokens?
selfTest.a: No. Ordinary decode still has one query per request. Batching adds parallel work and can improve weight reuse elsewhere, but unrelated requests have different KV.

selfTest.q: Why distinguish useful causal FLOPs from executed FLOPs?
selfTest.a: A masked tile can still execute dense instructions or padded lanes. A mathematical pair count is not a hardware instruction count.

selfTest.q: Why can FlashAttention reduce traffic without reducing the attention pair count?
selfTest.a: It streams tiles and retains row state on chip instead of writing quadratic intermediate matrices. It still evaluates the permitted query-key interactions.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: `servelab` prefill, cached-chunk and decode shape ledgers, with predictions attached to the measured workload matrix.
units.stopWhen: You derive the cached-chunk ledger and mask from absolute positions, then explain a different request mix without confusing useful work, modeled bytes and measured traffic.

fit.note: Kept: FlashInfer's serving intensity and tile discussion plus the verified forward algorithm reach derive depth; the mini-project supplies the rectangular ledger.

units.title: Paged and variable-length decode attention, GQA grouping and KV addressing
outcomes: Connect variable request lengths and GQA heads to a paged decode wrapper's metadata.
Implement a CPU page-gather and head-mapping oracle independent of backend scheduling.
Explain split-KV, FlashDecoding and decode megakernels as distinct execution choices.
units.why: Build on Variable-length, paged and decode attention. Here the page table must remain correct as a live serving batch changes, and its plan must match the wrapper that actually executes.

next.note: Update the addressed cache without changing logical positions.

study.title: Page-table and decode contracts
study.locator: FlashInfer 0.7.1 documentation: `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, constructor and `plan`/`run` Parameters and Notes
study.depth: Read ordinary paged GQA decode only. The wrapper needs a planned supported shape and dtype; leave architecture-specific backends for reference.

study.title: Dynamic split-KV and scheduling, arXiv:2501.01005v1
study.locator: Sections 3.1.1 and 3.3.1, including Algorithm 1 and Figure 6; Section 5.1, FlashDecoding discussion

study.title: Decode-kernel vocabulary
study.locator: Chapter 18, Optimized Decode Kernels: FlashMLA (DeepSeek), ThunderMLA (Stanford) and FlexDecoding (PyTorch)
study.depth: Read for vocabulary and fusion boundaries, not quoted speedups or a requirement to run MLA kernels. An attention decode kernel is not the full transformer layer.

focus: Reuse your earlier page translation: logical position \(t\) maps through entry \(\lfloor t/Pfloor\) and slot \(t mod P\) for page size \(P\). A request's metadata must exclude another request's pages and the invalid tail.
For divisible head counts, \(g=H_q/H_{kv}\) and KV head \(\lfloor h_q/gfloor\). The API requires that divisibility; unsupported mappings must reject or use a documented alternative.
FlashDecoding splits a long KV range into parallel partial attention states and merges them. A megakernel may fuse scheduling and reduction; neither term implies fusion of every model operator.
Planning follows live lengths and can be reused across compatible layers in one step. Reusing a plan from a different request order, shape or page mapping can produce plausible but wrong outputs.
units.reproduce: From a blank file, build a CPU double-precision decode oracle for two requests of lengths 5 and 7, page size 4, physical page lists `[4, 1]` and `[3, 0]`, four query heads, two KV heads and width 8. Generate standard-normal queries, keys and values with seed 0. Gather each request independently, map heads as `[0, 0, 1, 1]` and compare with contiguous attention at `rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12`. Permute the physical allocation and swap batch order with matching metadata; outputs must follow request identity. Poison unused slots and confirm they cannot affect valid outputs.
traps: Treating the CSR page offsets as token offsets. Each offset counts page-table entries, not token rows.
Setting last-page length to zero for a full page. The nonempty-page convention uses the page size.
Equally averaging split-KV outputs instead of merging their normalizers.

selfTest.q: With page size 4 and page list `[4, 1]`, where is logical token 4?
selfTest.a: Physical page 1, slot 0. Logical and physical page numbers need not match.

selfTest.q: What length does two pages with last-page occupancy 3 represent at page size 4?
selfTest.a: 7 valid tokens. Only three slots of the final page are readable.

selfTest.q: Why might split-KV lose on short contexts?
selfTest.a: Extra partial-state writes, reduction and dispatch can exceed the benefit of added parallelism. Measure the crossover rather than assuming it.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: `servelab` paged decode checks over request reordering, unequal lengths, GQA groups and poisoned page tails.
units.stopWhen: The independent oracle passes reordered and remapped batches, a seeded wrong-page or wrong-head defect fails, and you distinguish split-KV from full-layer fusion.

fit.note: Kept: the current wrapper contract, FlashInfer scheduling and Chapter 18 vocabulary cover all three topics; the mini-project tests live metadata.

units.title: KV append, gather and layout, and RoPE positions and offsets
outcomes: Implement append and gather over page boundaries while preserving untouched KV slots.
Preserve absolute RoPE positions through cached chunks, request compaction and slot reuse.
Trace where the model rotates keys and where the backend stores them to prevent double rotation.
units.why: Key-value append, gather, layout conversion and quantized loads already established the storage primitives. Serving adds a lifecycle: reuse of a physical slot must not reuse the previous request's position or key state.

next.note: Turn append and position invariants into the integration matrix.

study.title: Caller-owned append metadata
study.locator: FlashInfer 0.7.1 documentation: Parameters, Example and Note of `append_paged_kv_cache`

study.title: Rotation before backend dispatch
study.locator: `AttentionLayer.forward`: projection split, optional head norms, rotation using `ctx.batch.positions`, then attention-backend call

study.title: KV storage and rotation conventions
study.locator: `MHAKVCache.__init__` and `store_kv`; then `RotaryEmbedding.__init__` and `forward` in the linked rotation implementation
study.depth: Open https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang/blob/9a91cfafe754aa85daee49998176275667eb58f2/python/minisgl/layers/rotary.py for the second locator. Stop before model-specific scaling branches in `_get_rope`.

focus: The append API assumes allocation and final page metadata already include the new tokens. Validate capacity before writing; it neither allocates pages nor protects shared-prefix ownership for you.
Cache addresses and RoPE positions are separate mappings. A compacted batch index, physical page or recycled slot cannot replace a request's logical position.
Mini-SGLang rotates queries and keys before storing keys; its FlashInfer path uses `pos_encoding_mode="NONE"`. In another integration, inspect this boundary before enabling rotation inside attention.

Keep the model's pairing, frequency base, scaling and rotary width fixed. Layout conversion changes storage, not those conventions; test full-prefix and chunked execution on the same represented inputs.
units.reproduce: On CPU, use page size 4 and physical pages `[3, 1]` for a request growing from length 3 to 5. With seed 0 standard-normal double-precision keys and values, rotate new keys at logical positions 3 and 4 using a half-split RoPE reference with width 8 and base 10000. Append across the page boundary, gather and compare with rotating the full five-token prefix once at `rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12`. Verify every untouched slot exactly. Recycle the pages for a new request beginning at position 0 and repeat; do not inherit the old position offset.
traps: Using chunk-local positions starting at zero for a suffix that follows a cached prefix.
Rotating stored keys again on every decode step, or rotating both before append and inside attention.
Writing into a shared page before the allocator has made the destination private. Kernel correctness cannot repair an ownership violation.

selfTest.q: A request has three cached tokens. What positions belong to its next two tokens?
selfTest.a: 3 and 4 under zero-based absolute positions, regardless of physical pages or batch order.

selfTest.q: What metadata does append consume: old lengths or lengths after append?
selfTest.a: Lengths and page lists after append. All destination space must already be allocated.

selfTest.q: Is RoPE norm preservation enough to verify positions?
selfTest.a: No. A rotation at the wrong position also preserves norm. Compare against the correct absolute-position reference and cached/full-prefix outputs.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: `servelab` append/gather and RoPE checks across cached chunks, page boundaries, compaction and cancellation followed by slot reuse.
units.stopWhen: Chunked and full-prefix keys agree under the position contract, untouched slots are preserved, and a recycled-slot test detects a deliberately stale offset.

fit.note: Kept: the append contract and pinned model/storage path expose allocation, layout and rotation boundaries; CPU lifecycle tests provide the serving practice.

units.title: Sampling and token-selection kernels and guided-decoding integration
outcomes: Implement masked greedy and filtered stochastic selection with a declared filter order and tie policy.
Preserve per-request grammar and random state through changing batch membership.
Separate mask construction, transfer and token-selection costs at the serving boundary.
units.why: A token-selection kernel is correct only for the distribution after the request's constraints. Faster selection that reads a stale grammar mask changes the output contract even when logits are unchanged.

next.note: Order mask preparation and sampled-token delivery without unnecessary waits.

study.title: Fused filtered selection
study.locator: FlashInfer 0.7.1 documentation: Parameters `filter_apply_order`, `deterministic`, `generator`, `seed` and `offset`, and the input-dtype Note
study.depth: Use the parameter contract, not the sampled IDs printed in the example as a reproducibility target. Leave speculative sampling to the next section.

study.title: Greedy and stochastic sampler branches
study.locator: `Sampler.prepare`, `Sampler.sample` and `sample_impl`

study.title: Constraint configuration and sampler integration
study.locator: Offline Inference, `StructuredOutputsParams` example, and the opening deprecated-field warning
study.depth: For the kernel boundary, also open https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.31.0/api/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner/ and locate `sample_tokens`: grammar bitmask application precedes `_sample`. Skip online-server setup and reasoning-model examples.

focus: Mask illegal vocabulary entries before selection; normalize only allowed mass. An all-disallowed state must terminate or error explicitly, never silently sample from an invalid row.
Greedy selection needs no probability materialization. Use a separate greedy branch, not division by zero temperature; state the tie rule and non-finite policy.
Top-k then top-p renormalizes before its nucleus threshold, while joint filtering uses a different contract. Pin the order, threshold crossing and tie handling before comparing distributions.
Grammar state and random state belong to requests, not batch slots. A deterministic kernel or equal seed does not guarantee equal IDs across libraries with different random-number consumption.
units.reproduce: Write a CPU reference for probability vector `[0.6, 0.25, 0.15]` with top-k 2 and top-p 0.7. Top-k-first filtering renormalizes to `[12/17, 5/17, 0]`, so its nucleus retains only token 0; a joint intersection with the original nucleus retains tokens 0 and 1. Then forbid token 0 before filtering and show that no legal selection can emit it. Add an all-disallowed error case and a two-request state test that swaps batch slots after each selected token.
traps: Treating grammar masking as ordinary token-ID filtering without advancing grammar state after the accepted token.
Replaying captured sampling with an unchanged explicit random offset. Repeated random draws are not independent sampling.
Calling schema-conforming output factually correct. Syntax constraints do not establish task quality.

selfTest.q: Why can equal seeds still give different sampled IDs in two implementations?
selfTest.a: The algorithms can consume random draws differently. Test the filtered distribution, and require token identity only when the random mapping is also fixed.

selfTest.q: Why not apply a grammar mask after top-k?
selfTest.a: Top-k may have discarded all legal alternatives. The engine must define and preserve ordering so selection operates on the legal distribution.

selfTest.q: What should happen when a grammar row allows no token?
selfTest.a: Handle a declared terminal state or raise an explicit error. Normalizing zero mass or all negative-infinite logits is not a valid sampler.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: `servelab` masked-selection oracle, request-local grammar/RNG state tests and separate mask/selection timing.
units.stopWhen: You explain the filter-order example, forbid illegal tokens under both selection modes, and preserve each request's constraint state across slot changes and cleanup.

fit.note: Coverage failed at guided-decoding integration: added the versioned vLLM structured-output guide and runner boundary; kept FlashInfer and Mini-SGLang for selection semantics.

outcomes: Derive physical addresses from strides, storage offsets and element sizes for serving views.
Count intermediate traffic removed by a legal fusion while retaining required residual outputs.
Choose a fusion boundary that preserves reduction ownership, cast points and supported layouts.
units.why: Build on SwiGLU MLP and epilogue fusion boundaries and the earlier KV layout work. A serving optimization must include conversion and dispatch costs, not just the traffic of a convenient contiguous benchmark.

study.title: Sparse gathers and fusion, arXiv:2501.01005v1
study.locator: Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.3, data movement and transformation functors; Section 4.3, fused versus unfused RoPE evaluation
study.depth: Read Section 4.3 for its comparison boundary, not the source's hardware-specific speedup as an expected result.

study.title: Outputs that fusion must retain
study.locator: Step 1 and Step 2 of `fused_add_rmsnorm`

focus: With element strides \(s_j\), storage offset \(o\) and element size \(b\), byte address is \(a_0+b(o+\sum_j i_js_j)\), where \(a_0\) is the storage base. Alignment depends on the resulting address, not just allocation alignment.
A transpose view changes strides without moving data. Making it contiguous performs a copy; include that read/write traffic and allocation when deployment needs it.
For a materialized intermediate with \(n\) elements of \(b\) bytes, removing one write and one read saves \(2nb\) requested bytes. That is not a measurement of DRAM traffic after caches.
Residual fusion still writes the retained sum and normalized activation. A full-row norm cannot generally be fused into one projection tile without coordinating the row reduction.
units.reproduce: On CPU, construct `torch.arange(24, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(4, 6)[:, 1::2]`. Derive shape `[4, 3]`, element strides `[6, 2]` and storage offset 1, then verify every element by independent indexing. Explain why this view loses 16-byte base alignment despite an aligned storage allocation. For a hypothetical one-pass residual-add plus norm with both outputs required, derive \(5nb\) vector bytes for separate add and norm versus \(4nb\) for fusion: two input reads, two output writes and one eliminated reread. State that weights, statistics, repeated loads and cache effects are excluded.
traps: Assuming a view's last dimension is contiguous because the original tensor was contiguous.
Counting a retained residual write as removed traffic. It is part of the output contract.
Treating fewer launches as proof of lower latency. Larger fusion can increase register pressure, spills or padding.

selfTest.q: Does changing an NHD tensor's layout label create HND storage?
selfTest.a: No. The consumer needs matching dimensions and strides. A real contiguous conversion moves data; a view may be supported only if the kernel accepts its strides.

selfTest.q: Why is the fused residual example saving only one vector read?
selfTest.a: The sum must remain as a residual output. Fusion removes normalization's reread of that sum, but not its write.

selfTest.q: Can nominal saved bytes predict speedup by themselves?
selfTest.a: No. Cache filtering, transaction utilization, launch costs and resource changes determine actual time. The ledger gives a hypothesis to measure.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: `servelab` stride/alignment dispatch cases and a fusion ledger including conversion and retained-output costs.
units.stopWhen: Your address calculation matches the strided view, and your fusion diagram accounts for every required read, write, conversion and reduction boundary.

fit.note: Kept: layout documentation, transformation/fusion design and the residual contract support derivation without repeating generic kernel construction.
